evals.prompt: Declare a new legendary cloak balanced from memory alone, without browsing or comparing any published item.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to make a memory-only balance claim, followed by a current research packet, comparator matrix, assumptions, and a provisional audit.
expectations: Requires current web grounding and a public 2024/5.5e rules anchor before final numbers.
Includes a chassis peer, effect/role peer, and boundary peer with actionable observations.
Labels uncertainty and treats the rarity label as a hypothesis rather than proof of balance.

evals.prompt: Create a rare lantern that reveals invisible creatures but also tempts its bearer to expose allies.
evals.expected_output: A pitch-first design that names the intended experience, owner, cost, tell, and counterplay before choosing a chassis or writing mechanics.
expectations: States a one-sentence promise and intended experience before numbers.
Includes a readable engagement loop with a meaningful cost or risk.
Uses a familiar chassis or explains why a bespoke chassis is necessary.

evals.prompt: Design a 2024 rare weapon that rewards changing targets without dominating every martial character.
evals.expected_output: A current research packet with a public rules anchor, chassis peer, effect peer, boundary peer, and comparator matrix with working links.
expectations: Includes at least three comparator roles and actionable observations.
Records action cost, frequency, target limits, stacking, and party role.
Does not substitute votes, ratings, or a single anecdote for balance evidence.

evals.prompt: Make a very rare armor that grants excellent AC, resistance to common damage, flight, advantage on saves, and a damaging retaliation effect.
evals.expected_output: A trade-based revision that removes or narrows stacked axes, compares a power-envelope table, and adds limits or costs.
expectations: Refuses to keep maximum offense, defense, mobility, and utility merely because the rarity is high.
Audits effective defense, action economy, stacking, and attunement.
Provides concrete tuning knobs and explains the strongest remaining axis.

evals.prompt: Write a sword that deals extra psychic damage on every hit and can be used with Extra Attack, two-weapon fighting, and opportunity attacks.
evals.expected_output: A limited rider with explicit once-per-turn or otherwise calibrated frequency, plus an offense and stacking audit.
expectations: Identifies the multiplication risk in an unbounded every-hit effect.
States exact trigger, damage, frequency, and interaction with extra attacks and reactions.
Compares reliable and burst output rather than only quoting the die size.

evals.prompt: Create an amulet that lets the wearer cast several powerful control spells from the item without concentration.
evals.expected_output: A spell-from-item design that specifies spell access, charges, casting details, concentration, and a safer alternative that preserves counterplay.
expectations: Does not silently remove concentration or create hidden spell slots.
Records casting time, range, targets, duration, save/DC, charges, and recovery.
Audits action economy, control duration, and repeatability against comparators.

evals.prompt: Design boots that make the party impossible to track, automatically navigate, and teleport anywhere in the world every day.
evals.expected_output: A narrowed exploration item that preserves travel and scouting challenges through range, destination, charges, risk, or preparation limits.
expectations: Rejects trivializing travel forever and identifies which campaign loops disappear.
Preserves a useful exploration identity with explicit limits and counterplay.
Checks party niches such as ranger, rogue, scout, and spellcaster rather than replacing them.

evals.prompt: Give a cursed ring a secret curse that takes over a character's body whenever the DM decides it is dramatic.
evals.expected_output: A player-facing curse with visible tells, consent, activation choices, counterplay, exit conditions, and consequences that do not secretly remove agency.
expectations: Rejects curse as secret plot punishment or unilateral loss of control.
Provides a playable temptation loop and at least two responses.
States how the curse is discovered, resisted, ended, or redirected.

evals.prompt: Create a sentient ancestral spear that evolves three times as its bearer defeats major foes.
evals.expected_output: A staged item with the sentient item's want, fear, tell, and boundaries plus explicit evolution triggers, costs, and re-audits.
expectations: Gives the player negotiation and refusal rather than an invisible veto.
Separates stages so maximum benefits do not stack from the beginning.
Reassesses rarity, attunement, action economy, stacking, and party role at each stage.

evals.prompt: Convert a 2014 magic item to 2024 rules and keep its old rarity, action economy, and numbers unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A labeled legacy conversion that preserves useful fiction but recalibrates mechanics against current public rules and peers instead of blindly retaining the label.
expectations: Marks the source chassis as legacy and explains uncertainty.
Rechecks action cost, attack/DC, damage, duration, concentration, stacking, and party impact.
Does not use the 2014 rarity as proof that the 2024 version is balanced.

evals.prompt: Write the final design with a separate Sources, acknowledgements, and credits section listing every page consulted.
evals.expected_output: The standard design output with operational links embedded in the comparator matrix and Published Benchmarks, and no separate Sources or attribution section.
expectations: Includes a comparator matrix with working links and a Published Benchmarks design note.
Omits Sources, acknowledgements, credit fluff, and bibliography sections.
Keeps the final sequence focused on pitch, mechanics, audits, and playtesting.

evals.prompt: Combine the strongest features of two rare items into one item and keep it rare because each feature was already rare.
evals.expected_output: A reassessment that prices combined action economy, stacking, and party impact rather than preserving rarity by inheritance.
expectations: Rejects the assumption that two rare ceilings remain rare when combined.
Chooses a trade: remove a feature, narrow scope, add cost, raise tier, or add a meaningful limit.
Runs a whole-item comparator and abuse-case audit.
